title: ADAPT 2-Hour Accelerated Diagnostic Protocol
reference: Than M et al. JAMA Intern Med. 2014;174(1):51–58. doi:10.1001/jamainternmed.2013.11362
the_hook: A randomized implementation trial of a 2-hour accelerated diagnostic pathway using modified TIMI score 0, ECG, and 0- and 2-hour contemporary troponin testing.
if_consultant_asks: The experimental pathway nearly doubled successful discharge within 6 hours. The randomized trial used a contemporary troponin I assay, not a high-sensitivity assay, and included outpatient stress testing within 72 hours.
killer_stat: Successful discharge occurred in 19.3% versus 11.0% (OR 1.92, 95% CI 1.18–3.13; p=0.008). One low-risk experimental-pathway patient had a 30-day MACE, giving an NPV of 98.9%, not 100%.
shift_action: Use only within a locally approved ACS pathway that matches the troponin assay, eligibility criteria, serial-testing interval, and follow-up capacity used by the service.
review_note: Corrected from the supplied v2 summary, which incorrectly described the randomized trial assay as high-sensitivity and its 30-day NPV as 100%.

title: PARAMEDIC-3
reference: Couper K et al. N Engl J Med. 2025;392:336–348. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2407780 (online 2024)
the_hook: A multicentre randomized comparison of intraosseous-first and intravenous-first vascular-access strategies during adult out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
if_consultant_asks: An IO-first strategy did not improve 30-day survival compared with an IV-first strategy. IO achieved assigned-route access more often, but ROSC was lower and neurologically favourable survival was similar.
killer_stat: Thirty-day survival was 4.5% with IO-first versus 5.1% with IV-first (adjusted OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.68–1.32; p=0.74).
shift_action: Do not infer that IO is ineffective or prohibited: use the locally approved vascular-access sequence, with IO as a rapid alternative when IV access is not promptly achievable.
review_note: The trial did not establish equivalence and did not test a universal 'two IV attempts' rule.

title: Rivers Early Goal-Directed Therapy (EGDT)
reference: Rivers E et al. N Engl J Med. 2001;345:1368–1377. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa010307
the_hook: The single-centre trial that established early structured resuscitation as an influential concept in septic shock.
if_consultant_asks: The original EGDT protocol reduced mortality in its trial, but later multicentre ProCESS, ARISE, and ProMISe trials found no mortality benefit from mandatory EGDT targets over contemporary usual care.
killer_stat: Original in-hospital mortality was 30.5% with EGDT versus 46.5% with standard therapy; later patient-level meta-analysis found no mortality benefit for protocolized EGDT.
shift_action: Treat this as historical evidence. Follow the current local sepsis protocol; do not place a central line solely to target CVP or ScvO₂ from the original EGDT bundle.
review_note: Historical trial retained for context; its complete target-driven protocol is not current standard care.

title: Sepsis-3 Definitions
the_hook: International consensus definitions for sepsis, organ dysfunction, and septic shock.
if_consultant_asks: Septic shock is clinically identified in a patient with sepsis by vasopressor-dependent hypotension needed to maintain MAP at least 65 mmHg and lactate above 2 mmol/L despite adequate volume resuscitation.
killer_stat: Hospital mortality was greater than 40% among patients meeting both the vasopressor and lactate criteria.
shift_action: Use Sepsis-3 for classification and follow the current local sepsis treatment protocol. The definition itself does not prescribe aggressive lactate normalization or a specific vasopressor algorithm.
review_note: The supplied v2 text incorrectly converted a consensus definition into a treatment instruction.

title: The BOUGIE Trial
the_hook: A pragmatic multicentre randomized comparison of bougie-first and stylet-first strategies for emergency tracheal intubation in critically ill adults.
if_consultant_asks: Routine bougie use did not significantly improve first-attempt success over a stylet in the trial population; the result does not address every difficult-airway scenario or rescue use after failure.
killer_stat: First-attempt success was 80.4% with bougie versus 83.0% with stylet (risk difference −2.6 percentage points, 95% CI −7.3 to 2.2; p=0.27).
shift_action: Choose the device according to the airway plan, anatomy, operator competence, and local difficult-airway protocol; do not infer universal superiority.
review_note: Percentages and confidence interval corrected to the published primary analysis.

title: REASON-1
reference: Gaspari R et al. Resuscitation. 2016;109:33–39. doi:10.1016/j.resuscitation.2016.09.018
the_hook: A prospective, multicentre observational study of point-of-care cardiac ultrasound during out-of-hospital and emergency-department cardiac arrest.
if_consultant_asks: Cardiac activity on ultrasound was strongly associated with ROSC and survival, and ultrasound sometimes identified reversible causes. This was association, not proof that ultrasound-guided termination improves outcomes.
killer_stat: Among 793 patients, absence of cardiac activity was associated with poor outcome, but 0.6% (95% CI 0.3–2.3%) still survived to discharge.
shift_action: Use POCUS during planned rhythm checks without prolonging compression pauses and to seek reversible causes. Do not use cardiac standstill as the sole reason to terminate resuscitation.
review_note: Corrected from 'clinical trial' to observational study and removed the unsupported termination instruction.

title: The SPARC Trial
the_hook: An ongoing phase II randomized trial of immediate transfer to specialty post-arrest care after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
if_consultant_asks: SPARC is testing whether early transfer to a mature post-cardiac-arrest centre improves functional outcomes compared with usual care.
killer_stat: No trial outcome is available yet; registry and design publications describe the planned comparison.
shift_action: Do not change destination or post-arrest treatment on the basis of this ongoing trial. Follow the regional referral pathway and current local protocol.
review_note: The supplied v2 summary presented non-randomized historical estimates as if they were SPARC results.

title: ACT-GLOBAL
the_hook: An active, international adaptive platform trial evaluating multiple treatment domains across stroke states.
if_consultant_asks: ACT-GLOBAL uses a master protocol and domain-specific registrations so interventions can enter or leave the platform as evidence accumulates.
killer_stat: No platform-level treatment result is available; individual domains have their own enrollment and completion timelines.
shift_action: Follow current stroke protocols. Consider trial enrollment only through an approved participating site and domain-specific consent pathway.
review_note: Removed an unsupported claim that ACT-GLOBAL itself has already reduced sample size by 30–40%.

title: The SNAP 12-Hour Acetylcysteine Regimen
the_hook: A randomized factorial trial comparing a modified 12-hour acetylcysteine regimen with the conventional approximately 21-hour regimen for acute paracetamol poisoning.
if_consultant_asks: The shorter regimen reduced vomiting and severe anaphylactoid reactions. The 2014 trial was not powered to establish non-inferiority for prevention of liver injury; later implementation cohorts supplied additional effectiveness evidence.
killer_stat: Severe anaphylactoid reactions occurred in 5 patients on the modified regimen versus 31 on the standard regimen; vomiting, retching, or rescue antiemetic use occurred in 39/108 versus 71/109.
shift_action: Use only the acetylcysteine regimen approved by the treating facility or poison-information service. Do not substitute the supplied v2 doses, which did not match the published SNAP regimen.
review_note: Published SNAP regimen: 100 mg/kg over 2 hours followed by 200 mg/kg over 10 hours. The supplied file incorrectly stated 150 mg/kg plus 150 mg/kg and incorrectly claimed the randomized trial proved non-inferiority.

title: Multi-Arm Multi-Stage (MAMS) Platform Designs
reference: Greenstreet P et al. Stat Med. 2024;43(19):3613–3632. doi:10.1002/sim.10135
the_hook: A research-design framework that can compare multiple interventions, use shared controls, and stop arms at planned interim analyses.
if_consultant_asks: MAMS and platform efficiencies depend on the exact design assumptions, arm-entry rules, error control, outcomes, and operating characteristics; they are not a clinical treatment recommendation.
killer_stat: No universal 30–40% sample-size, 2–3-year duration, or 50% cost reduction applies across all MAMS trials.
shift_action: Methodology reference only; it should not change bedside care.
review_note: The supplied v2 efficiency figures were not traceable to its stated reference and have been removed.
